comment: Dex's authproxy connector reads its trusted X-Remote-* headers inside handleConnectorCallback (server/handlers.go), which serves /callback/{connector} — NOT /auth/{connector}, which merely creates the AuthRequest and redirects here. This is where the browser's Kratos session must actually be checked.

/auth and /auth/{connector} only create the AuthRequest and redirect to /callback/{connector} (server/handlers.go's handleConnectorLogin) — no trusted headers are read here, so no cookie_session check is needed. See dex-authproxy-callback for where the actual header check happens.

Server-to-server Dex discovery endpoint that the authproxy connector never inspects — no browser cookie is available on this call, so it must not require cookie_session. Split into one rule per path (rather than a /dex/<**> catch-all, or a pipe-alternation glob, which Oathkeeper's glob matching strategy does not support) to avoid overlapping with dex-authproxy-callback's /dex/callback<**> match — Oathkeeper requires exactly one rule match per request.
Server-to-server code/refresh-token exchange — see dex-passthrough-wellknown comment.
JWKS endpoint used to verify ID token signatures — see dex-passthrough-wellknown comment.
OIDC userinfo endpoint — see dex-passthrough-wellknown comment.
